data.comment: Filter operator

data.name: FilterOperatorNotAvailable
data.comment: {0} = data type of the column, e.g. CLOB

data.name: FilterEmptyTextIsNull
data.value: Empty text is NULL in Oracle – use “{0}”.
data.comment: {0} = the filter operator "is NULL" (OperatorIsNull)

data.name: NotANumber
data.comment: {0} = the value as typed

data.name: NotADate
data.comment: {0} = the value as typed. The format hint describes the input format the filter parses (day.month.year), only the letters are translated.

data.name: NotAHexValue
data.value: “{0}” is not a hex value (e.g. CAFE01).
data.comment: {0} = the value as typed

data.name: ColumnDoesNotExist
data.comment: {0} = column name

data.name: ColumnNotSortable
data.comment: {0} = column name

data.name: FkConditionInList
data.comment: Key condition of an FK jump from several rows. {0} = column name, {1} = the first values, separated by "; ", {2} = number of values

data.name: FkSkippedRowsOne
data.comment: Note on an FK jump from several rows (no final period). {0} = number of rows (1)

data.name: FkSkippedRowsOther
data.comment: Note on an FK jump from several rows (no final period). {0} = number of rows

data.name: FkColumnMissing
data.comment: Why an FK jump is not possible. {0} = column name

data.name: FkJumpTypeNotSupported
data.comment: Why an FK jump is not possible. {0} = data type of the key column

data.name: FkKeyIsNull
data.comment: Why an FK jump is not possible. {0} = column name

data.name: FkColumnNullInAllRows
data.comment: Why an FK jump is not possible. {0} = column name, {1} = number of selected rows

data.name: FkKeyNullInAllRows
data.value: Key ({0}) is NULL in all {1:N0} rows.
data.comment: Why an FK jump is not possible. {0} = key columns, separated by ", ", {1} = number of selected rows

data.name: FkSeveralRowsNeedSingleColumnKey
data.value: With several rows, only possible for single-column keys.
data.comment: Why an FK jump is not possible

data.name: FkTooManyValues
data.comment: Why an FK jump is not possible. {0} = number of distinct key values, {1} = maximum

data.name: FkValueContainsSeparator
data.value: A value contains “{0}” – not possible with several values.
data.comment: Why an FK jump is not possible. {0} = the list separator of the filter bar (;)

data.name: SqlRejectForUpdate
data.value: SELECT … FOR UPDATE locks rows – FerretSharp only sets locks when editing.
data.comment: Why the SQL editor does not run a statement

data.name: SqlRejectTruncate
data.value: The SQL editor does not run TRUNCATE: it deletes every row and cannot be undone. Use DELETE instead – it stays in the transaction.
data.comment: Why the SQL editor does not run a statement

data.name: SqlRejectPlSqlObject
data.value: The SQL editor does not create PL/SQL objects (procedures, functions, packages, triggers, types) yet.
data.comment: Why the SQL editor does not run a statement: CREATE [OR REPLACE] PROCEDURE …

data.name: SqlRejectDdlBinds
data.value: DDL takes no bind variables (:{0}) – write the value into the statement.
data.comment: Why the SQL editor does not run a statement. {0} = name of the first bind variable, without the colon

data.name: SqlRejectPlSql
data.value: The SQL editor does not run PL/SQL blocks or procedure calls – they can commit on their own.
data.comment: Why the SQL editor does not run a statement

data.name: SqlRejectTransactionControl
data.value: Use the status bar for {0} (Commit, Rollback).
data.comment: Why the SQL editor does not run a statement. {0} = first word of the statement, e.g. COMMIT

data.name: SqlRejectSessionControl
data.value: ALTER SESSION/SYSTEM changes the workspace’s session and is not run.
data.comment: Why the SQL editor does not run a statement

data.name: SqlRejectLock
data.value: LOCK TABLE is not run – FerretSharp only sets locks when editing.
data.comment: Why the SQL editor does not run a statement

data.name: SqlRejectExplain
data.value: Use the “Plan” button for execution plans.
data.comment: Why the SQL editor does not run EXPLAIN PLAN. “Plan” is the label of the button in the SQL editor's toolbar.

data.name: SqlRejectOther
data.value: The SQL editor does not run “{0}” – only SELECT, WITH, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and MERGE.
data.comment: Why the SQL editor does not run a statement. {0} = first word of the statement

data.name: SqlPlanReadOnly
data.value: {0} changes data – the workspace is read-only.
data.comment: {0} = first word of the statement, e.g. UPDATE

data.name: SqlPlanReadOnlyDdl
data.value: {0} changes the schema – the workspace is read-only.
data.comment: {0} = first word of the DDL statement, e.g. CREATE

data.name: SqlPlanDmlBeforeDdl
data.value: {0} (DDL) would commit the changes of statement {1} implicitly. Put the DDL before the DML or run them separately.
data.comment: A script has DML before DDL. {0} = first word of the DDL statement, e.g. CREATE; {1} = number of the DML statement in the script

data.name: SqlPlanStatementProblem
data.comment: A script was not run. {0} = number of the statement in the script, {1} = why (a full sentence)

data.name: BindValueMissing
data.comment: SQL editor variable. {0} = name of the bind variable (shown with its colon)

data.name: BindNumberMissing
data.value: :{0}: number missing (for NULL, choose the type NULL).
data.comment: SQL editor variable. {0} = name of the bind variable

data.name: BindNotANumber
data.comment: SQL editor variable. {0} = name of the bind variable, {1} = the value as typed

data.name: BindDateMissing
data.value: :{0}: date missing (for NULL, choose the type NULL).
data.comment: SQL editor variable. {0} = name of the bind variable

data.name: BindNotADate
data.value: :{0}: “{1}” is not a date (DD.MM.YYYY [hh:mm[:ss]] or ISO).
data.comment: SQL editor variable. {0} = name of the bind variable, {1} = the value as typed. The format hint describes the input format (day.month.year).

data.name: BindNotAHexValue
data.value: :{0}: “{1}” is not a hex value (e.g. CAFE01).
data.comment: SQL editor variable. {0} = name of the bind variable, {1} = the value as typed

data.name: BindUnknownType
data.comment: SQL editor variable. {0} = name of the bind variable

data.name: BindValueMasked
data.comment: Shown instead of a bind value of a Prod connection

data.name: CompletionSynonym
data.comment: Detail of an autocomplete entry. {0} = OWNER.NAME of the object the synonym points to

data.name: CompletionPublicSynonym
data.comment: Detail of an autocomplete entry for a public synonym. {0} = OWNER.NAME of the object the synonym points to

data.name: CompletionTable
data.comment: Detail of an autocomplete entry: the object is a table

data.name: CompletionView
data.comment: Detail of an autocomplete entry: the object is a view

data.name: CompletionMaterializedView
data.comment: Detail of an autocomplete entry: the object is a materialized view

data.name: InsertExportHeaderOne
data.comment: First comment line of an INSERT script. {0} = number of rows (1), {1} = OWNER.TABLE

data.name: InsertExportHeaderOther
data.comment: First comment line of an INSERT script. {0} = number of rows, {1} = OWNER.TABLE

data.name: InsertExportAmpersand
data.value: Contains '&': run SET DEFINE OFF first in SQL*Plus.
data.comment: Comment line in an INSERT script

data.name: InsertExportIdentity
data.value: {0} is an identity column: GENERATED ALWAYS rejects explicit values (ORA-32795).
data.comment: Comment line in an INSERT script. {0} = column name

data.name: InsertExportSkipped
data.comment: SQL comment in place of a value of an INSERT script. {0} = data type, {1} = size or type of the value, e.g. "5,000 characters"

data.name: DmlPrimaryKeyNull
data.comment: {0} = column name

data.name: DmlRowWithoutKey
data.value: The row has no key and cannot be written.
